analysis.investment_thesis: Swasth Foodtech fails the Magic Formula on both legs: ROE of 0.17% implies near-zero ROIC, and with negligible earnings there is no meaningful earnings yield at an INR 8.88 Cr market cap. A commodity refined-oil micro-cap started in 2021 with no track record is precisely the kind of stock a systematic quant screen should reject.
key_strengths: Promoter holding healthy at 72.89% — skin in the game
Operates in FMCG/edible oils, a consumption-linked space
Small base could theoretically allow high % growth if execution improves
key_risks: ROE of 0.17% → ROIC effectively zero, failing the 'good business' leg
Negligible earnings make EBIT/EV uncomputable and likely unattractive
Refined oils is a low-margin, capital-intensive commodity with pricing pressure
red_flags: Only 5 years old (incorporated 2021), no 3-year ROIC track record
Micro-cap (INR 8.88 Cr) with thin liquidity and disclosure
Commodity refined-oil business with structurally thin margins
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The Magic Formula ranks companies on two axes — return on capital (quality) and earnings yield (price). Swasth Foodtech fails the quality leg outright: ROE of 0.17% means the business is essentially not earning anything on shareholder capital, and ROIC will be in the same ballpark, nowhere near my 20%+ threshold. Without a meaningful EBIT figure, the earnings yield (EBIT/EV) is effectively non-computable — and at an INR 8.88 Cr market cap on near-zero profits, it is almost certainly below my 12% hurdle on any normalized basis. Both legs of the formula fail.

Beyond the metrics, refined edible oils is a commodity business dominated by scale players (Adani Wilmar, Ruchi, Marico, Emami Agrotech) where gross margins are razor-thin and pricing tracks crude palm/soy. A 2021-incorporated micro-cap has no moat, no track record of sustained ROIC, and no cost advantage. Systematic investing means no storytelling — the numbers here say avoid, full stop.
